title: Distinguishing different psychiatric disorders using DDx-PRS.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Zenodo record 10.5281/zenodo.15019356 (the only accession text-mined from the paper) via its API: one file, DDxPRS-v1.0.2.zip, 154 KB, GPL-3.0, described as the R code release; no data. Read the GitHub README: the tool takes per-person PRS (polygenic risk scores, a weighted sum of risk alleles) that the user must compute on their own genotyped test sample. Europe PMC full text for the paper (PMC13559851) and the preprint (PMC10862992) both returned HTTP 500; the supplementary-files endpoint returned a non-zip; the PMC preprint page showed only the abstract.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Training data are public PGC (Psychiatric Genomics Consortium) GWAS (genome-wide association study) summary statistics, total n = 1,048,683; held-out test data are 11,460 genotyped individuals from PGC cohorts with SCZ/BIP/MDD/control diagnoses (abstract only). That PGC individual-level genotypes require a PGC secondary-analysis application or dbGaP access is known PGC policy, not read in this paper's data statement, which I could not retrieve.

a1_downloadable.note: The only labelled per-person data (11,460 test individuals with genotypes and diagnoses) are PGC cohort data, which need a PGC secondary-analysis proposal or dbGaP (NIH controlled-access database) application; the Zenodo deposit is code only (checked). Controlled access, so A1 fails.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No public table pairs a diagnosis label with per-person features; public GWAS summary statistics are per-SNP effect sizes, not per-person examples. The label would only exist after obtaining controlled-access cohorts.

a3_inputs_present.note: Per-person PRS must be computed from individual genotypes (PRS-CS plus PLINK per the README); genotypes are not public.

a4_units_stated.note: Not checked in files; README states PRS are on the liability scale after a stated transformation.

a5_enough_rows.note: Paper reports 11,460 test individuals (abstract only); no row count verified because no file is accessible.

a6_fits_laptop.note: A four-column PRS table for 11,460 people would be tiny, but it is not available; genotype-level work would be far larger.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot be checked: no data file is accessible.

a8_label_provenance.note: Diagnoses are clinical (cohort ascertainment), not model outputs; per paper text only.

existing_models.name: DDx-PRS (this paper), an R function combining case-control PRS with clinical priors to give posterior diagnosis probabilities
existing_models.score_and_split: Abstract reports good calibration on 11,460 held-out individuals from cohorts not in training, with equal numbers per category; exact numbers not retrieved (full text unavailable).

backbone.name: none suitable (genotype-derived PRS are tabular; no open-weight sequence backbone applies to per-person polygenic scores)
backbone.licence: Code GPL-3.0 (checked on Zenodo); data controlled access

integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Not usable for a per-person model without controlled-access genotypes.

honest_claim_h3: Without controlled-access PGC genotypes, no per-person model can be trained or tested; only the published summary-statistics method can be rerun on someone else's data.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a person's genetic risk scores for several psychiatric disorders to predict which diagnosis they have.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-person genetic risk scores for schizophrenia, bipolar disorder and depression; the paper's 11,460 test individuals are not publicly downloadable.
plain_idea.predict: Clinical diagnosis category (schizophrenia, bipolar, depression or control) recorded by the contributing cohorts.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Psychiatrists could use genetic evidence to sharpen early differential diagnosis, but the labelled data sit behind a consortium access process.

ml_idea: Learn a multiclass classifier on multi-disorder PRS versus DDx-PRS's analytic posterior; infeasible because per-person labelled data are controlled access.

effort.cheapest_killing_check: Zenodo listing (done): code-only 154 KB zip, no per-person data.

verdict_reason: A1 fails: the only labelled per-person data (11,460 PGC individuals with genotypes and diagnoses) are controlled access via PGC/dbGaP application, and the Zenodo deposit is code only (verified). Public GWAS summary statistics give no per-person examples, so A2 and A3 fail too.
